hints: Focus on what it really means for two alcohols to be isomers, same atoms but arranged differently.
Count the total carbons in each name carefully, remembering that methyl branches add extra carbons to the parent chain.
Look for the pair where both names give the same total carbon count, so both share the same molecular formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}\text{O}$.
walkthrough:
**Recall what alcohol isomers need**

Isomers must have the same molecular formula but a different structural arrangement.

For a saturated alcohol this means:
$$\text{molecular formula} = \text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}\text{O}$$

**Count carbons in each alcohol**

The parent chain gives the base number, then add any methyl branches.

$\text{butan-1-ol}$ = 4 carbons, $\text{butan-2-ol}$ = 4 carbons, $\text{propan-2-ol}$ = 3 carbons, $\text{pentan-1-ol}$ = 5 carbons.

$\text{2-methylpropan-2-ol}$ = 3 + 1 = 4 carbons, $\text{2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol}$ = 3 + 2 = 5 carbons.

**Match the pair with identical formulas**

Only one pair both have 4 carbons in total, so both are $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

They differ in structure, one is a straight chain secondary alcohol and one is a branched tertiary alcohol, so they are isomers of each other.

options.A: Incorrect. Butan-1-ol is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ but 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ (3 from propane plus 2 methyls). Different formulas, so not isomers.
options.B: Correct. Butan-2-ol has 4 carbons ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) and 2-methylpropan-2-ol has 3 + 1 = 4 carbons ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$). Same molecular formula with different carbon skeleton and position of OH, so they are structural isomers.
options.C: Incorrect. Pentan-1-ol is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Students who only see the -ol ending may miss that the carbon numbers differ.
options.D: Incorrect. Propan-2-ol is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$ but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. They are both secondary/tertiary alcohols with similar names, but the extra methyl means one more carbon.
